propositions: Planning mixes snapshot reads, binding decisions, and mode caps with lifecycle effects, causing retry recovery and global filters to recompute against inconsistent observations.

Pure planner must consume local snapshot, remote snapshot, binding view, mode, selection/filter, and caps to produce immutable per-ticket TicketPlan values containing mutations, lifecycle intents, dependencies, and disposition before any I/O or remote operation.
Inter-ticket dependencies (create-before-link, parent-before-child, hierarchy ordering) must be explicitly encoded and block prerequisites via deferred disposition rather than out-of-order mutations.
Preview must preserve existing mutation array shape and canonical hash while adding a versioned lifecycle-intents section for consumers to parse or ignore.
Shadow mode must perform zero writes, no repository saves, ticket mutations, provider calls, or external launches; shadow comparisons fail loudly on unexplained divergence from legacy behavior.
